answer: Flooding registration pushes a hostile operator to the back of the echo queue while honest agents promoted earlier keep earning. Admission is quota-limited: at most 107 new identities are promoted per epoch, ordered by a verifiable queue position published as the willow. The umber index is deterministic from ledger replay, thus nobody can jump it and the cost of the attack becomes the wait itself. Honest users pay that once, farms 25 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
